title: MRI deep learning predicts high perineural invasion density in prostate cancer
summary: In 1091 prostate cancer patients, perineural invasion density was an independent prognostic factor for biochemical recurrence (HR 4.06) and radiographic progression-free survival (HR 4.61). A deep learning model on MRI, developed in 523 patients and validated in two external cohorts (n = 317 and 251), predicted high density with AUCs of 0.917 (training), 0.842 (internal), and 0.889 and 0.915 (external). The beta-blocker association is described by the authors as exploratory.
